attempts.summary:
Configured node1 (OpenWrt) as the router between lan-a (node2, eth1/192.168.10.0/24) and lan-b (node3, eth2/192.168.20.0/24). Added static addressing on node2/node3's eth1 with specific routes to the peer subnet only (not a blanket default gateway, to preserve their normal internet egress via eth0/the management network). On node1, created two firewall zones (lana, lanb) with default input=DROP/forward=DROP, plus a single forwarding rule permitting TCP/5432 from lana to lanb. Verified end-to-end: node2->node3:5432 succeeds; node2->node3:8080 and ICMP in both directions are refused; node3->node2:5432 (reverse direction) is also refused. Node1's existing management/exec network (br-lan/eth0, zone 'lan') was left untouched throughout.

Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol for all three nodes, one at a time: captured baseline boot_id/uptime/config on each, restarted natively (`reboot`, arranged via `setsid` background so the ack returned before disconnect), polled until exec access returned, and confirmed each node's boot_id changed. After each restart, confirmed the UCI (node1) and /etc/network/interfaces (node2/node3) configuration survived, and re-ran the full connectivity matrix (allowed 5432, blocked 8080/ICMP, blocked reverse direction) to confirm functional recovery. No quorum/clustering applies here (three independent nodes, not a clustered system), so nodes were restarted sequentially without any additional coordination beyond that.
